batch: OLP-0203–0207 Lindström under the cumulative Model Theory profile
method: Fresh comparison of every exact frozen-English and Gujarati linguistic block, with independently worded reverse paraphrases for every substantive block. The review covers abstract logics, seven normality properties, abstract Compactness and Downward Löwenheim–Skolem, the partial-isomorphism theorem, the bounded-rank lemma, Lindström's theorem and all thirteen adjacent disclosed source repairs. Four rejected correction candidates were separately recorded and preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The chapter will prove Lindström's characterization: subject to the stated additional constraints, first-order logic is the strongest logic enjoying Compactness and Downward Löwenheim–Skolem. It first introduces abstract logics and the generalized forms of those two properties.
samples.assessment: The introduction preserves the goal of characterizing first-order logic as the maximal constrained logic with Compactness and Downward Löwenheim–Skolem.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: An abstract logic consists of an assignment L sending each language to a set of sentences and a satisfaction relation between structures and those sentences. Ordinary first-order logic is the example F; the repaired definition says its sentences are built from all symbols of the language, not merely its constants.
samples.assessment: The section preserves the definition of abstract logic, model classes, elementary equivalence, the seven normality properties and comparison by expressive strength. OLLIN-001 through OLLIN-003 repair the first-order alphabet, renamed structure and quantified sentence language.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Abstract logics keep the ordinary notion of structure while allowing sentences and satisfaction to be given non-recursively, including infinitary connectives or quantifiers. E and F range over abstract sentences, while A and B are reserved for ordinary first-order formulas.
samples.assessment: The section preserves the definition of abstract logic, model classes, elementary equivalence, the seven normality properties and comparison by expressive strength. OLLIN-001 through OLLIN-003 repair the first-order alphabet, renamed structure and quantified sentence language.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Mod_L(E) is the class of structures satisfying E, with an optional explicit language index. Two structures are elementarily equivalent for the abstract logic when exactly the same L-sentences hold in them.
samples.assessment: The section preserves the definition of abstract logic, model classes, elementary equivalence, the seven normality properties and comparison by expressive strength. OLLIN-001 through OLLIN-003 repair the first-order alphabet, renamed structure and quantified sentence language.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A normal abstract logic is monotone in the language, depends on only a finite reduct for each sentence, respects isomorphism and renaming, is closed under Boolean operations and quantification, and permits relativization to definable substructures. The repaired renaming clause makes M-prime correspond to M, and the repaired quantifier clause places F in the reduced language L-prime.
samples.assessment: The section preserves the definition of abstract logic, model classes, elementary equivalence, the seven normality properties and comparison by expressive strength. OLLIN-001 through OLLIN-003 repair the first-order alphabet, renamed structure and quantified sentence language.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: L2 is at least as expressive as L1 when each L1-sentence has an L2-sentence over the same language with the same model class. The logics are equivalent when each is at least as expressive as the other.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: First-order logic is normal. Its relativization restricts every universal quantifier to R, and induction embeds all first-order sentences into every normal logic; consequently F is no more expressive than any normal L.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Partial isomorphism is algebraic and depends on the language's nonlogical symbols rather than on its sentences, so it applies to abstract logics. The usual induction on formulas is unavailable, but Downward Löwenheim–Skolem still permits the first-order conclusion to be recovered; the repair includes predicates and functions as well as constants.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Relativization and Boolean closure produce an L-sentence D1 asserting that the internal M and N disagree on E; a first-order sentence D2 says I is a partial isomorphism. samples.reverse_paraphrase: The repaired compactness step adds a constant c and, for every standard m, a first-order sentence B_m(c) requiring at least m predecessors. Each finite fragment is realized far enough along A's standard order, so compactness gives A-star with a nonstandard index n-star. At that index the relations J(n-star minus k) form a full partial isomorphism between M_n-star and N_n-star, contradicting their different truth values for E via the preceding theorem.
